extracted.intended_audience: public commenters, immigration stakeholders, practitioners (immigration attorneys, advocates), and analysts reviewing the DHS proposed public-charge rule
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing comments or analysis in response to the DHS proposed public-charge rule (preamble and economic analysis), including scrutiny of population estimates, cost assumptions, procedural changes (forms and RFEs), and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population projection method (5-year average)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the projected annual average total population subject to public charge review using the 5-year average of annual estimated totals (fiscal years 2012–2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The estimate is based on DHS Yearbook of Immigration Statistics data; DHS provides ranges across years (lowest and highest annual estimates) and welcomes public comments on these population estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from inadmissibility review based on public charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain classes of admission are exempt from public charge inadmissibility review for applicants seeking adjustment of status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table(s) present counts of exempt individuals; DHS notes further discussion of exempt classes in the preamble and invites comment on estimates of exempt populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from requirement to submit an affidavit of support
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain classes of admission are exempt from the requirement to submit an affidavit of support for admission, adjustment of status, or registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an affidavit of support is submitted, a contract is established between the sponsor and the U.S. Government to establish a legally enforceable obligation to support the applicant financially. DHS provides estimates of populations exempt versus required to submit affidavits and invites comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of population for estimates (in‑US applicants only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Population estimates are based on immigrants present in the United States who are applying for adjustment of status, not immigrants outside the United States undergoing consular processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS emphasizes this distinction repeatedly when inviting comments on population estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of nonimmigrants seeking extension/change of status
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes to conduct reviews of nonimmigrants applying for extension of stay or change of status to determine whether the applicant has received, is receiving, or is likely to receive public benefits as defined in the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS proposes officers could exercise discretion about issuing an RFE (request for evidence); such applicants would not automatically be required to file Form I-944 unless an RFE is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt of public benefits alone not dispositive
rubrics_metrics.description: Past or current receipt of public benefits, alone, would not justify a finding of inadmissibility on public charge grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as a limiting principle in the proposed review of public benefits receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity cost of time — primary proxy ($10.66/hour)
rubrics_metrics.description: For most populations (e.g., many adjustment applicants), DHS uses federal minimum wage plus weighted average benefits of $10.66 per hour as a proxy for time valuation to estimate opportunity costs of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This $10.66 = $7.25 federal minimum wage * 1.47 benefits-to-wage multiplier. DHS welcomes public comments on use of $10.66 per hour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity cost of time — alternate proxy ($35.78/hour)
rubrics_metrics.description: For some populations (such as those submitting an affidavit of support), DHS uses the unweighted mean hourly wage of $24.34 multiplied by the benefits-to-wage multiplier to estimate $35.78 per hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS assumes these populations are dispersed across occupations; invites public comments on this assumption and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits-to-wage multiplier calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS calculates a benefits-to-wage multiplier of 1.47 using BLS data: (Total Employee Compensation per hour) / (Wages and Salaries per hour) = $36.32 / $24.77 = 1.466 ≈ 1.47.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to convert wages to total compensation when estimating opportunity costs of time (includes paid leave, insurance, retirement, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline definition for cost–benefit analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The baseline estimate of current costs is defined by assuming 'no change' to DHS regulations (i.e., current operations and requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline includes current costs associated with completing and filing Form I-485, required biometrics and medical exam (Form I-693), any affidavits of support, and requested fee waivers (Form I-912). DHS compares proposed rule provisions to this baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of costs included in analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs considered include filing fees, opportunity cost of time (OCT), biometrics services fee, biometrics OCT, biometrics travel costs, medical exam cost, postage costs, and related incidental costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS details per-form breakdowns (I-485, I-693, I-129, I-129CW, I-539, affidavits, fee waivers) and identifies which populations incur which components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions for biometrics burden and travel
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS assumes average roundtrip distance to an ASC is 50 miles, roundtrip travel time 2.5 hours, average wait for service 1.17 hours, for a total biometrics-related time burden of 3.67 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biometrics services processing fee is $85 per applicant; travel cost per trip calculated at GSA POV reimbursement rate $0.545/mile yields $27.25 per trip; DHS assumes each applicant travels independently to ASC. DHS computes OCT for biometrics using $10.66/hour for most populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time burden to complete Form I-485
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS estimates the time burden of completing Form I-485 is 6.25 hours per response, including reviewing instructions, gathering required documentation, completing the application, preparing statements, attaching documentation, and submitting the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute opportunity cost of time per applicant (6.25 hrs * chosen hourly rate) and aggregate OCT across estimated population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form fees and fee computations (example: I-485)
rubrics_metrics.description: The current Form I-485 filing fee is $1,140; DHS calculates annual aggregate filing cost by multiplying fee by estimated annual population (e.g., $1,140 * 382,264 = $435,780,960).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS presents similar fee*population calculations for other forms and components in the baseline cost table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical examination requirement and cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS requires most applicants filing Form I-485 to submit Form I-693 completed by a civil surgeon; DHS assumes applicants pay all medical exam costs directly to providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS notes exam fees vary widely ($20–$1,000) and assumes an average cost of $490 for analysis; costs include any follow-up tests or treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of application outcome statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: When tabulating receipts/approvals/denials, 'denials' include applications that were denied, terminated, revoked, or withdrawn; cases may be adjudicated in a later year than the one received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This note clarifies DHS counting methods for form-based population estimates (I-129, I-129CW, I-539 receipts/approvals/denials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretionary use of RFEs to require Form I-944
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes that determinations for nonimmigrants seeking extension/change of status would not require Form I-944 by default; USCIS officers could exercise discretion to issue an RFE requiring Form I-944.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits automatic documentation burdens and places decision to request Form I-944 in officer discretion; DHS explicitly states past/current benefits receipt alone is insufficient for inadmissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement that analyzed costs are current (not additional)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS reiterates that costs examined in the section are not additional costs imposed by the proposed rule but are costs applicants currently incur as part of the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies the baseline vs incremental cost framing in the economic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of data sources for estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS uses USCIS internal data (Office of Performance & Quality), DHS Yearbook of Immigration Statistics, BLS reports, and Paperwork Reduction Act supporting statements as sources for population and cost estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS cites specific tables and sources (Yearbook Table 7, BLS Employer Cost for Employee Compensation, PRA supporting statements) and invites comment on data and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation for public comment on assumptions and estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS explicitly welcomes public comments on estimates of populations subject to public charge review, exemptions, and on cost assumptions (e.g., use of $10.66/hr and $35.78/hr for opportunity cost of time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders are encouraged to provide data or critique assumptions used in the population and economic analyses.
